author: t-jankowski
title: Windows CC build fails with compiler/linker out-of-memory errors under high parallelism
signature: Windows Release build runs out of memory - compiler fatal error C1060 (out of heap space) and linker fatal error LNK1102 (out of memory) under high parallelism|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Conditional Compilation
failed_jobs.symptom: cl.exe fatal error C1060: compiler is out of heap space across multiple MSVC compile units (onednn, low_precision_transformations, frontends)

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_windows_cc
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregate status job reports failure because the Conditional Compilation build job failed

key_errors: c1xx : fatal  error C1060: compiler is out of heap space [...\openvino_build\src\common\low_precision_transformations\openvino_lp_transformations_obj.vcxproj]
cl : command line  error D8027: cannot execute 'C:\BuildTools\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.42.34433\bin\HostX64\x64\c1xx.dll' [...\openvino_lp_transformations_obj.vcxproj]
C:\BuildTools\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.42.34433\include\type_traits(1817,106): error C1060: compiler is out of heap space [...\onednn\src\common\dnnl_common.vcxproj]
C:\BuildTools\MSBuild\Microsoft\VC\v170\Microsoft.CppCommon.targets(755,5): error MSB4018: The "CL" task failed unexpectedly. [...\openvino_common_translators.vcxproj]
root_cause: The Windows Conditional Compilation build runs MSVC cl.exe with high parallelism (multiple .vcxproj compiling concurrently via MSBuild) on a Windows runner with constrained memory. Several heavy translation units (oneDNN, low_precision_transformations, core/op headers pulled into frontends common_translators) exhaust the compiler process's available heap space simultaneously, causing cl.exe to abort with C1060 across several concurrent projects, which then cascades into the overall build failure and the downstream status-aggregation job. This is the same recurring MSVC resource-exhaustion failure already tracked 20 times in the pattern database; it is not caused by the merged PR (#38771, an RTTI hash fix) touching build-heavy translation units.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible outside CI; requires the same Windows runner memory/CPU configuration and build parallelism. Locally: build the CC (BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF, SELECTIVE_BUILD=COLLECT -> ON) configuration with MSVC under constrained RAM (<=16GB) and high /MP or CMake parallel job count to approximate the heap exhaustion.
recommended_actions: Reduce MSBuild/CMake parallelism (-j / /maxcpucount) for the Windows CC job, or split heavy projects (oneDNN, low_precision_transformations, frontends common_translators) into separate build stages.
Move the Windows CC runner to a larger-memory SKU, or set /Zm (increase compiler memory allocation) and disable PCH where not needed for the largest translation units.
Consider enabling ccache/sccache for Windows CC to reduce the number of cl.exe processes that must run concurrently from a cold cache.
Escalate to the CI infra team: this exact pattern (C1060 on Windows CC) has recurred 20 times since 2026-11-03; a permanent infra fix (runner sizing or parallelism cap) is overdue.
prevention_strategies: Cap concurrent MSVC compile jobs on memory-constrained Windows runners, add a /Zm compiler flag bump, and consider a scheduled check that alerts if Windows CC heap-exhaustion failures recur within a rolling window, independent of which commit triggered the run.
historical_context: Matches an existing pattern (signature_hash 80cfa127185fbf3e, 'Windows CC build fails with compiler/linker out-of-memory errors under high parallelism') first seen 2026-11-03 and now observed 20 times, most recently just before this run at https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/actions/runs/45167302131. This failure is unrelated to the code changes in the merging PR (#38771) across all prior occurrences, confirming it is an infrastructure/resource-sizing issue rather than a code regression.
